sheets.prompt:
Create ONE polished photographic CONTACT SHEET containing EXACTLY SIX distinct portrait photographs, in 3 columns by 2 rows, for choosing the hero image of a British vegetable-growing book's "Vegetable Troubles" section. This is an image-selection sheet, NOT a book page layout.
Use reference 2 ONLY as the contact-sheet FORMAT and photographic style guide: equal portrait panels, each roughly 185:240 aspect ratio, thin warm-white gutters and a warm-white number strip below each photograph. Whole sheet almost square landscape, about 1320x1194 or larger. Label the six panels with simple black numerals 1, 2, 3 on the first row and 4, 5, 6 on the second row, outside the photographs. No other text, no chapter titles, no oval contents overlay, no logo, no captions.
Reference 1 is the user's SPECIFIC earlier image 21, a RED CABBAGE. In panel 1 faithfully adapt that exact composition: compact purple cabbage head, blue-green outer leaves with purple veins, another cabbage behind at upper right, green mesh near upper left, soil near lower right. Keep the recognisable plant, viewpoint, colours and scale. Show somewhat more obvious but believable CATERPILLAR feeding damage to selected outer leaves: irregular torn holes of mixed sizes and nibbled margins, unequally distributed, with veins sometimes remaining. Keep the main purple head attractive and largely intact. A single small realistically sized large-white caterpillar may sit on an outer leaf if it reads naturally; reference 3 provides caterpillar appearance, never enlarge it disproportionately.
Panel 2: a different close garden view of a GREEN CABBAGE with one naturally curled, blue-green leaf catching soft side light, irregular caterpillar-chewed holes and one small yellow-green black-speckled caterpillar along a vein. Include enough whole-plant context for a beautiful portrait opener, not a scientific macro plate.
Panel 3: BROAD BEANS growing in place, low close view of the fresh shoot tip bearing a credible cluster of small black bean aphids on the tender upper stem, larger mature leaves and perhaps one bean pod below. Background green foliage softly recedes; realistic scale and understated damage, no giant insects.
Panel 4: COURGETTE growing in a natural soil bed, a recognisable courgette fruit and flower near its base, one broad foreground leaf with irregular dusty-white patches of powdery mildew over its green surface. Distinguish powdery surface patches from natural silvery vein markings. Healthy younger leaves behind. Do not blanket every leaf uniformly.
Panel 5: loose-leaf LETTUCE growing in dark garden soil, natural slug/snail feeding holes in one or two lower leaves and a single modestly sized brown garden snail at the lower leaf edge. Crisp lettuce greens, tactile leaf edges, plant is the subject, not a giant snail.
Panel 6: TOMATOES attached to a natural vine in a greenhouse, close side-low viewpoint exposing the blossom end of one prominent green-to-blushing fruit with a characteristic local dark sunken blossom-end-rot patch opposite the stalk; a few healthy fruit behind. Keep plant anatomy and attachments plausible; no rot spread on foliage.
Overall: convincing high-quality editorial garden photography, like a real UK allotment or home vegetable patch in soft daylight. Strong single subject per panel, living crops growing in situ, natural asymmetry, imperfect leaves, quietly varied planting backgrounds, realistic soil. Visually inviting despite visible trouble. Rich natural colours, fine real textures, gentle depth of field, modest contrast. No fantasy plants, no pristine symmetrical arrangements, no harvest piles, no stylised rendering, no dramatic horror, no clinical labels, no hands or people. Make the six compositions clearly different and legible at contact-sheet size. Preserve all SIX complete portrait frames.

Create ONE photographic contact sheet with EXACTLY SIX distinct portrait photographs arranged 3 columns by 2 rows. This is the second choice sheet for a British vegetable-growing book's "Vegetable Troubles" opener.
Reference 1 shows the exact contact sheet format to MATCH: equal tall portrait panels around185:240, narrow warm-white gutters and a separate number strip BELOW every picture, approximately1320x1194 overall or larger. Label top row 7,8,9 and bottom row10,11,12 in simple black numerals on those strips. These six numbers are the ONLY text. No chapter title, no contents panel, no oval overlay, no diagnostic labels, no additional frames. Keep all six photos complete.
Reference 2 is the user's original earlier image21 red cabbage. Use it to create panel7: FAITHFULLY retain the compact purple cabbage head with blue-green purple-veined leaves, neighbouring cabbage upper right and green netting upper left. Preserve its original low close viewpoint, lighting and natural texture. Outer leaves show noticeable but MODERATE uneven caterpillar feeding holes and nibbled margins. Keep the purple heart healthy and intact. This is a subtle alternative to panel1 of reference1: NO VISIBLE caterpillar or other insect. Do not over-shred the plant. All damage should look naturally chewed, with irregular shapes and sizes, not stamped holes.
Panel8: CURLY PURPLE KALE growing outdoors in a normal garden bed, a shapely plant with purple stems and a rich mixture of grey-green and purple curly leaves. A few upper outer leaves have irregular caterpillar holes and missing patches at margins; young central growth mostly intact. Frame a whole recognisable plant with dark soil and quietly blurred nearby vegetables. Natural plant geometry, no hybrid cabbage head.
Panel9: LEEKS growing in a garden soil bed, fairly close low portrait view along overlapping long flat blue-green leaves. One or two foreground leaves have scattered tiny raised orange rust pustules, variable spots rather than a perfect pattern, some local yellowing. Older and younger leaves vary, whole planting still natural and attractive. No caterpillars here, no holes, no gigantic fungus. Background recedes among healthy leek foliage.
Panel10: SWISS CHARD in a raised garden bed, red and cream stems at soil level, one recognisable broad green foreground leaf showing irregular pale tan papery leaf-miner blotches INSIDE the leaf tissue, only part of the leaf affected. Other leaves healthy, softly lit. Botanical realism, natural asymmetric leaf contours. Do not turn blotches into round holes or artificial painted polygons.
Panel11: YOUNG RADISH plants growing in situ in a modest kitchen-garden row, camera low and close, lobed true leaves and the modest reddish shoulder of one root near the soil surface. Several leaves carry small scattered flea-beetle shot holes, tiny and uneven, mixed with healthy leaves. The whole crop group fills the portrait with believable soil at bottom and subdued plants behind, no giant isolated insects.
Panel12: PEAS growing on ordinary green support netting, one close plant with a couple of natural pods, tendrils and paired pale-green leaves with repeated but UNEVEN small semicircular pea-and-bean-weevil notches around some leaf margins. Calm natural garden depth, pods credible size and attached at nodes. No extra holes in the leaf centres, no visibly oversized insect. Composition wider and more airy than a macro, recognisable peas in place.
All panels are natural editorial PHOTOGRAPHS, not illustration or CGI. Soft British daylight, realistic colour, tactile surface textures, natural variation and modest depth of field. Crops growing where they live, no staged harvests, no perfect symmetry, no hands or people. Show visible gardening troubles yet keep each frame attractive enough for a book section opener. Distinct crop silhouettes and backgrounds; give each picture one strong focal subject. Do not reuse the other five crops of reference1; reference1 is primarily the matching photographic style and layout.

review: Both generated sheets visually inspected: six portrait panels each, continuous numbering 1–12, original red-cabbage composition recognisable in 1 and 7. Selection concepts only; refine insect scale, plant anatomy and diagnostic detail when developing a chosen full-size photograph.
production_gate: No paid subscription or upscale at this stage. Before printer upload if adopted: produce/upscale chosen artwork, inspect fine detail and verify at least 300 ppi at final placement. DPI metadata alone is insufficient.

storage: Generated images are displayed and saved automatically by the image generation workflow; these project records retain exact prompts, references and local output paths.
